title: Pollution regulation on plant total factor productivity

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
- Method: Difference-in-Differences (DID) with two-way fixed effects (unit and period). Event-study interactions are used to assess pre-trends.
- Why: Treatment is assigned based on being above the emissions threshold (treated=1) and activated by the regulation in period 4 (post=1 for t ≥ 4). We observe treated and control plants before and after the regulation, enabling DID.
- Key identification assumptions:
  - Parallel trends: In the absence of the regulation, average TFP trends for high- and low-emission plants would have evolved in parallel.
  - No anticipation: Treated plants did not adjust TFP before period 4 in anticipation of the policy.
  - Stable composition and SUTVA: No changes in the composition of treated/control groups across time; no spillovers across plants.

We estimate a TWFE DID: y_it = α_i + δ_t + β (treated_i × post_t) + ε_it. β is the average treatment effect of the regulation on TFP for high-emission plants. We also:
- Check pre-trends via an event-study (treated × period dummies, with unit and period FE).
- Run a placebo DID with an artificial earlier policy date.
- Add unit-specific linear trends as a robustness check.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Load packages
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(lmtest)
  library(sandwich)
})

# 1) Read data
df <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s07_data.csv")

# Basic checks
if(!all(c("unit_id","period","treated","post","treat_x_post","y") %in% names(df))){
  stop("Data does not contain the required columns.")
}

# 2) Main DID: TWFE with cluster-robust SE (cluster at unit level)
did_mod <- lm(y ~ treat_x_post + factor(unit_id) + factor(period), data = df)
vc_unit <- vcovCL(did_mod, cluster = df$unit_id, type = "HC1")
did_res <- coeftest(did_mod, vcov. = vc_unit)
main_coef <- did_res["treat_x_post", "Estimate"]
main_se   <- did_res["treat_x_post", "Std. Error"]
main_t    <- did_res["treat_x_post", "t value"]
main_p    <- did_res["treat_x_post", "Pr(>|t|)"]

cat("MAIN DID (TWFE, cluster by unit):\n")
cat(sprintf("  Coef on treated x post = %.4f (SE = %.4f), t = %.2f, p = %.4f\n",
            main_coef, main_se, main_t, main_p))

# 3) Robustness A: Event-study style pre-trend check
#    y ~ factor(period):treated + unit FE + period FE
es_mod <- lm(y ~ factor(period):treated + factor(unit_id) + factor(period), data = df)
vc_es  <- vcovCL(es_mod, cluster = df$unit_id, type = "HC1")

# Extract all interaction terms factor(period)k:treated (or treated:factor(period)k)
terms_all <- names(coef(es_mod))
extract_period <- function(term){
  if(grepl("^factor\\(period\\)[0-9]+:treated$", term)){
    return(as.integer(sub("^factor\\(period\\)([0-9]+):treated$", "\\1", term)))
  } else if(grepl("^treated:factor\\(period\\)[0-9]+$", term)){
    return(as.integer(sub("^treated:factor\\(period\\)([0-9]+)$", "\\1", term)))
  } else {
    return(NA_integer_)
  }
}
period_of_term <- vapply(terms_all, extract_period, integer(1))
idx_es <- which(!is.na(period_of_term))
es_periods <- period_of_term[idx_es]
es_b <- coef(es_mod)[idx_es]
es_se <- sqrt(diag(vc_es))[idx_es]

# Pre-periods: 1,2,3; Post-periods: 4-8
pre_idx <- which(es_periods %in% c(1,2,3))
post_idx <- which(es_periods %in% c(4,5,6,7,8))

# Print pre-trend estimates
if(length(pre_idx) > 0){
  cat("EVENT STUDY (Differential effects by period; unit & period FE; cluster by unit):\n")
  for(i in pre_idx){
    cat(sprintf("  Pre-period %d differential (treated vs control): coef = %.4f (SE = %.4f)\n",
                es_periods[i], es_b[i], es_se[i]))
  }
  # Joint Wald test: pre-period coefficients = 0
  b_pre <- es_b[pre_idx]
  V_pre <- vc_es[idx_es[pre_idx], idx_es[pre_idx], drop=FALSE]
  # Handle potential singularity gracefully
  if(all(is.finite(b_pre)) && nrow(V_pre) == length(b_pre)){
    # Regularized inversion if needed
    eig <- eigen(V_pre, symmetric = TRUE)
    eig$values[eig$values < 1e-12] <- 1e-12
    V_pre_inv <- eig$vectors %*% diag(1/eig$values) %*% t(eig$vectors)
    wald_stat <- as.numeric(t(b_pre) %*% V_pre_inv %*% b_pre)
    df_wald <- length(b_pre)
    p_wald <- pchisq(wald_stat, df = df_wald, lower.tail = FALSE)
    cat(sprintf("  Joint pre-trends test (H0: all pre-period diffs = 0): chi2(%d) = %.2f, p = %.4f\n",
                df_wald, wald_stat, p_wald))
  }
  # Report average post effect (informal dynamic DID summary)
  if(length(post_idx) > 0){
    avg_post <- mean(es_b[post_idx])
    cat(sprintf("  Average post-period differential (periods 4-8): %.4f\n", avg_post))
  }
}

# 4) Robustness B: Placebo DID with fake policy date (pretend policy starts at period 3)
df$post_placebo <- as.integer(df$period >= 3)
df$treat_x_placebo <- df$treated * df$post_placebo
placebo_mod <- lm(y ~ treat_x_placebo + factor(unit_id) + factor(period), data = df)
vc_placebo  <- vcovCL(placebo_mod, cluster = df$unit_id, type = "HC1")
placebo_res <- coeftest(placebo_mod, vcov. = vc_placebo)
placebo_coef <- placebo_res["treat_x_placebo", "Estimate"]
placebo_se   <- placebo_res["treat_x_placebo", "Std. Error"]
placebo_p    <- placebo_res["treat_x_placebo", "Pr(>|t|)"]
cat("PLACEBO DID (fake start at period 3, cluster by unit):\n")
cat(sprintf("  Coef on treated x placebo_post = %.4f (SE = %.4f), p = %.4f\n",
            placebo_coef, placebo_se, placebo_p))

# 5) Robustness C: Add unit-specific linear trends
df$period_num <- df$period
trend_mod <- lm(y ~ treat_x_post + factor(unit_id) + factor(period) + factor(unit_id):period_num, data = df)
vc_trend  <- vcovCL(trend_mod, cluster = df$unit_id, type = "HC1")
trend_res <- coeftest(trend_mod, vcov. = vc_trend)
trend_coef <- trend_res["treat_x_post", "Estimate"]
trend_se   <- trend_res["treat_x_post", "Std. Error"]
trend_p    <- trend_res["treat_x_post", "Pr(>|t|)"]
cat("DID WITH UNIT TRENDS (TWFE + unit-specific linear trends, cluster by unit):\n")
cat(sprintf("  Coef on treated x post = %.4f (SE = %.4f), p = %.4f\n",
            trend_coef, trend_se, trend_p))

# 6) Alternative SE: Cluster by period (for main DID)
vc_period <- vcovCL(did_mod, cluster = df$period, type = "HC1")
did_res_period <- coeftest(did_mod, vcov. = vc_period)
alt_coef <- did_res_period["treat_x_post", "Estimate"]
alt_se   <- did_res_period["treat_x_post", "Std. Error"]
alt_p    <- did_res_period["treat_x_post", "Pr(>|t|)"]
cat("MAIN DID with alternative clustering (by period):\n")
cat(sprintf("  Coef on treated x post = %.4f (SE = %.4f), p = %.4f\n",
            alt_coef, alt_se, alt_p))

# 7) Final printed numerical result (primary estimate)
cat("\nPRIMARY ESTIMATE (preferred TWFE DID, cluster by unit):\n")
cat(sprintf("  Effect of tightened regulation on log TFP (treated vs control after period 4) = %.4f\n", main_coef))
```

## 3. Expected Findings
- Sign: Negative. Tightened air quality regulation likely imposes compliance costs and process adjustments that reduce measured TFP in the short to medium run.
- Magnitude: A modest decline in log TFP of about −0.03 to −0.08 (i.e., 3%–8%), averaging across post-policy years, with larger effects closer to implementation (periods 4–5). Event-study pre-trends should be statistically indistinguishable from zero. Placebo should show no significant effect, and adding unit-specific trends should not overturn the negative sign.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: DID — treated=above-threshold plants, control=below-threshold; shock=tighter regulation
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: High-emission plants experience productivity decline after regulation tightening
